property_summary: After calling beginFlashGovernanceAsset, configured remains the same as before the call.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, configured should be true (but the bug sets it to false).
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, configured must remain true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with a funded caller whose pendingFlashDecision is expired, the configured state stays unchanged (remains true).
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved that reverts (due to insufficient allowance), the configured state variable remains unchanged.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address is the same as the address passed to setDAO in the reference, but zero in the buggy version.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the value of DAO on the contract is always the same as it was before the call.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address is never set to a non-zero value unless the caller was a governed address or the DAO itself.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved from a non-DAO/non-governed address, the governer address remains zero.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governer address is never zero unless it was previously zero and the caller was either a governed address or the DAO itself.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governer address is non-zero if and only if the caller is a governed address or the DAO itself.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, if the DAO address was non-zero before the call, it remains the same as before.
After assertGovernanceApproved is called, the governed mapping value for every address k that was set via setGoverned remains false (i.e., never becomes true).

For any caller, after calling assertGovernanceApproved with the same sender and target, the governed status of the caller must equal its initial value (the reference correctly only changes governed for addresses in the isGoverned array, while the bug inverts it).
For any address k that is NOT in the governables array, the governed status of k remains unchanged after a call to assertGovernanceApproved from any sender.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, for any address in the governables array, the governed mapping at that address matches the boolean value passed in the isGoverned array.

After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the value returned by c.governed(k) must equal the bitwise-xor of the corresponding isGoverned array element and the boolean true (i.e., it must be the original isGoverned value, not its negation).

For any array element at index i, after a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governed status of governables[i] equals the value originally passed in isGoverned[i] (the reference preserves it, the bug inverts it).
For any valid caller, after a successful assertGovernanceApproved call, the governed mapping for the caller remains unchanged from before the call.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved on any sender that is already a governed address, the sender's governed status remains unchanged.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the caller's governed status is unchanged from its value before the call.
For any address caller that is not the DAO, after a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governed status of the caller remains unchanged.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the governed status of the caller is the same as before the call.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any parameters, the governed mapping for the msg.sender remains false if it was never set to true.
The governed mapping for an address can only be set to true by calling setGoverned with that address; otherwise it remains false.
Calling setGoverned with any address array and corresponding bool array should update the governed mapping for each address to the given bool.
When asserting governance approval for a sender, the sender must have been previously authorized by being listed as governed via setGoverned.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the mapping governed should remain unchanged (i.e., no new entries are added) regardless of the parameters.
After assertGovernanceApproved reverts, the setGoverned mapping for the target address remains equal to its pre-call value.
The `setGoverned` mapping for the contract address (this) remains unchanged after a call to `assertGovernanceApproved` from the contract itself.
When assertGovernanceApproved reverts, no entry in the governed mapping is added or updated for the target address.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping for msg.sender remains unchanged from its initial value.
The transferFrom call always succeeds, so the original contract always requires emergency or epoch check, while the mutant may skip the transfer.

The contract enforces that if the flash governance config has a positive lock time, then after a successful assertGovernanceApproved call, the pending decision's unlockTime must be strictly greater than the current block timestamp.

After assertGovernanceApproved, if flashGovernanceConfig.asset is the zero address, pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].asset remains zero only if caller is neither DAO nor governed, otherwise it becomes non-zero.

After a successful assertGovernanceApproved call, the unlockTime in pendingFlashDecision for that target and sender must be at least block.timestamp plus the configured flashGovernanceConfig.unlockTime.
After assertGovernanceApproved completes, pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].asset is non-zero if and only if the caller is the DAO or governed.
After a successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the pending unlock time for the decision is greater than or equal to the block timestamp (since it adds block.timestamp).
After assertGovernanceApproved returns without revert, security.lastFlashGovernanceAct is set to block.timestamp.
After assertGovernanceApproved returns without revert, the flash governance epoch timer is updated to the current block timestamp.
After successful assertGovernanceApproved, the epoch timestamp equals or exceeds lastFlashGovernanceAct, preserving the original invariant in C.
After a single call to assertGovernanceApproved that does not revert, the pendingFlashDecision unlockTime for the (target, sender) pair is strictly less than the block timestamp multiplied by two.
